headline: A quiet start to Samvat 2083 as foreign money floods back

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Monday, the ninth of November, and this is your Market Brief for the first full week of Samvat 2083.

Three things matter most this morning. First, the new Samvat began on a quiet note. In Sunday's Muhurat session the Sensex and Nifty slipped marginally, a rare red Diwali, though smaller companies did well.

Second, foreign money is pouring back in. Foreign institutional investors have put close to 46,000 crore rupees into Indian shares in just five sessions of November, as a sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks on Wall Street sends investors looking for other markets.

And third, it's a big week for inflation data, with both American and Indian numbers due, while the conflict between the US and Iran still hangs over oil and gold.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Now to how markets closed. In the one-hour Muhurat session on Sunday evening, the Sensex rose more than 400 points early on and the Nifty crossed 25,100. But the gains faded after the closing auction. The Sensex ended down about 29 points at 80,999, and the Nifty lost 44 points, about a fifth of a percent, to close at 24,986. Livemint notes the Sensex has ended Muhurat trading lower only eight times in thirty years.

The broader market told a different story. The smallcap index gained about 1 percent, and the midcap index edged up. Pharma and media stocks rose, while banks and realty dragged. Divi's Laboratories was the star, jumping 6 to 7 percent to a record 10,950 rupees after a 64 percent jump in quarterly profit. Tata Steel gained around 3 percent after steady results, and Sun Pharma rose for a fourth straight session. Finolex Cables shot up 14 percent. And Zee Entertainment jumped as much as 11 percent after saying its board will meet on the twelfth of November to consider a buyback or an interim dividend. HDFC Bank slipped to about 784 rupees, though it gained 13 percent over the past week.

Sunday's dip ended a seven-session winning streak. The week before was the Nifty's strongest weekly gain since February 2021, powered by foreign inflows, lower oil prices and solid earnings.

For today, GIFT Nifty was trading near 25,018, up about 38 points, pointing to a slightly positive start. Analysts quoted by Moneycontrol see 25,200 as the first hurdle for the Nifty, then 25,500. On the downside, 24,800 is immediate support, followed by the 24,300 to 24,400 zone. Sudeep Shah of SBI Securities says the bullish view holds as long as the Nifty stays above 24,750. For Bank Nifty, the level to watch is 58,700. It's a holiday-shortened week, and the commodity market stays shut on Tuesday morning for Balipratipada.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
Now to IPOs and deals. Two names have filed draft papers with the market regulator, SEBI. Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings, the parent of Coca-Cola's Indian bottling arm, has filed for an IPO that is entirely an offer for sale of nearly 99.75 crore shares, with listing planned in 2027. And IL Jin Electronics, a subsidiary of Amber Enterprises, has filed for a 2,500 crore rupee IPO. That one is all fresh issue, and the money will mainly go to cutting debt.

In corporate actions, Bosch has approved a one-for-five stock split and a three-for-one bonus issue. Together, one share would become twenty, each with a face value of 2 rupees. That still needs shareholder approval.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
Now the results roundup, starting with the big picture. Neelesh Surana of Mirae Asset says that of the roughly 80 percent of companies that have reported for the September quarter, revenue and operating profit have each grown 21 percent, and net profit 20 percent. He expects index earnings to grow about 18 percent this financial year.

In pharma, Divi's Laboratories reported a 64 percent jump in net profit, and the market loved it. In metals, Tata Steel's net profit rose 16 percent from a year ago.

Cables had a strong quarter. Finolex Cables' profit climbed 67.5 percent to 273 crore rupees, and revenue rose 65 percent to 2,269 crore, on higher cable volumes. RR Kabel's profit grew nearly 56 percent and revenue about 52 percent, though its subdued guidance for the year had weighed on the stock.

In batteries, Exide's profit surged 54 percent on strong demand and price hikes, while higher input costs dragged Amara Raja down. Both are investing heavily in lithium-ion.

In consumer goods, Dabur's profit rose 12 percent to about 499 crore rupees, while Emami's slipped about 2 percent to 145.5 crore. Both announced dividends.

And in telecom, Tata Teleservices Maharashtra narrowed its quarterly loss to 59 crore rupees, as revenue grew 8.4 percent.

Coming up this week, MRF and Cochin Shipyard are among the companies due to report.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
Now to the economy and policy. The rupee has drawn support from the foreign inflows. Analysts quoted by Business Standard say it could strengthen to 92 to the dollar if the US-Iran conflict eases, while government bond yields may trade between 7 and 7.5 percent, given inflation risks and the possibility of rate hikes.

A worrying sign from the farms. Rabi sowing is down 46 percent from last year. As of the thirtieth of October, crops covered 37.6 lakh hectares, against 69 lakh a year earlier. Oilseeds and pulses are worst hit, after a 48 percent rainfall deficit in October and lower reservoir levels. India's October inflation number is due this week. On the other hand, Indian sugar output data points to less need for imports, and raw sugar futures in New York fell as much as 3.5 percent.

On tax, Budget wish lists are arriving. FICCI wants the long-term capital gains tax on listed securities scrapped, with a higher securities transaction tax on delivery trades to make up the revenue. SBI Research has a similar idea. It proposes no tax on gains held over three years, a 2 lakh rupee exemption, and a 50 percent rise in transaction tax, and puts the cost at 40,000 to 50,000 crore rupees in the next financial year.

The GST Council has also proposed ending arrest powers under Section 69 of the GST law, while keeping prosecution and penalties. Parliament would need to amend the law.

Two more numbers. HSBC estimates India's data centre push could add 105 billion dollars to the import bill, though foreign investment in the sector could help the rupee over time. And the India-UK trade deal is showing up in the data. Imports of bulk Scotch whisky jumped nearly a thousand percent to 12.4 million dollars in August, the first full month of the pact.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Around the world, Wall Street is grappling with a rout of about 5.7 trillion dollars as bets on artificial intelligence unwind. Worries about valuations, debt and the returns on AI spending have been building, and the Democrats' sweep of Congress in the midterms has raised fears of curbs on data-centre expansion. Economist Gita Gopinath warned that nearly a trillion dollars of expected AI spending this year could be hard to recover, and flagged a risk of recession in the US.

That sell-off is partly India's gain. Investors are rotating into out-of-favour Asian markets, India and China among them, helped by easing inflation and trade tensions.

This week in America, October consumer inflation is due on Tuesday and producer prices on Friday, with several Federal Reserve officials speaking. On Iran, President Trump confirmed fresh military strikes, while saying Washington had made a lot of progress in talks with Tehran. Analysts expect that to keep oil and bullion volatile.

And Berkshire Hathaway spent 9.6 billion dollars buying back its own shares in the September quarter, even as operating earnings fell 5.8 percent to 12.7 billion dollars.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Now, your money. With Diwali here, a few tax points. Gifts in kind from your employer are tax-free if they total less than 15,000 rupees, but cash bonuses are taxed as salary. Money gifted by parents and other specified relatives is tax-free, but Livemint suggests documenting the transfer and reporting it in your return.

Two tribunal rulings worth noting. The Ahmedabad bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal deleted a 4.42 lakh rupee penalty on Nascent Info Technologies. The tax officer had disallowed 7.16 lakh rupees of employees' provident fund and ESI contributions that were deposited late, and then levied a penalty for misreporting income. The tribunal held that a disallowance alone does not establish misreporting. And in Surat, the tribunal gave relief to a farmer in an 18.24 lakh rupee land valuation dispute, directing the officer to examine the Departmental Valuation Officer's report. That could help buyers challenge high stamp duty valuations.

The RBI has clarified that existing cheque books will remain valid after the thirty-first of December, dismissing viral claims of new rules.

On gold, prices have fallen 24 percent globally from their January peak, but only 20 percent in India, because of import duty, a weaker rupee and unusually high premiums back in January. The World Gold Council thinks gold may be nearing an interim bottom. If you're looking at jewellers' gold savings schemes this Diwali, check how they work and the risks first.

Several fund houses, including HDFC, ICICI Prudential and Quant, have revised the risk ratings on some schemes this month, so it's worth checking yours. And a warning: fake loan apps are pushing instant credit offers on WhatsApp and social media this festive season. Bank branches are also closed today in some cities for Diwali and Govardhan Puja, so check before you head out.

That's the brief. Today, watch whether the Nifty can hold 24,800 and get past 25,200, whether the foreign buying continues, and how Wall Street's AI sell-off evolves. Later this week come the American and Indian inflation numbers, results from MRF and Cochin Shipyard, and Zee's board meeting on Thursday. A happy and prosperous Diwali to you, and have a good day.
